principle: Intelligence is a depreciating resource; governance is an accumulating asset.
routing_objective: For every task, use the lowest-cost intelligence that has demonstrated sufficient reliability under current governance.

classes.definition: Deterministic or nearly deterministic edits, transformations, extraction, formatting, bounded template work.
Execute well-specified blueprint slices with bounded code generation and tests.
Diagnose concrete failures from evidence, logs, tests, and receipts; propose bounded repairs.
Independently review governance, blueprint completeness, implementation claims, evidence quality, and hidden contradictions.
Convert founder intention into complete executable decision trees and anticipate failure branches, dependencies, and acceptance.
classes.requires_frontier: when free evidence proves lower classes insufficient

classes.definition: Unusually difficult future thinking, impossible-room exploration, second/third-order consequence analysis, novel synthesis, and high-impact challenge.

assignment_rule: Models are assigned to capability classes from measured LifeOS evidence, not brand, price, or historical prestige.
promotion_rule: A model may enter a higher capability class when controlled receipts show sufficient reliability for that class.
demotion_rule: A model must be demoted for a class when current-version evidence falls below threshold or repeated governance/reliability failures occur.
version_rule: Model versions are immutable benchmark identities. Never overwrite a prior version's history when a new version appears.
depreciation_rule: Re-evaluate class assignments whenever materially better/cheaper/free models become available. A previously frontier capability may become IMPLEMENTER or MECHANICAL economics without changing governance.
governance_asset_rule: Blueprints, failure history, verifiers, SENTRY tests, hard gates, receipts, and measured model evidence accumulate and must be preserved even as models are replaced.
